## PLAN ROUND 1 · publish · task first-edition

**Facts found**
- Three of the five runbooks name internal hosts or secret paths:
  - `runbooks/disk-full.md` step 1 names the host `db-primary-01.int.example.net`.
  - `runbooks/cert-expiry.md` step 1 names the secret path `secret/platform/acme-token`.
  - `runbooks/queue-backlog.md` step 1 names the host `jobs-01.int.example.net`.
- `runbooks/deploy-rollback.md` and `runbooks/dns-failure.md` name no host or secret.
- You use `runbooks/dns-failure.md` "when internal names stop resolving". A site served by name
  from an internal host may not load during that incident.
- `scripts/check.sh` enforces two rules:
  - The first line of every `runbooks/*.md` starts with "Use when".
  - Every `./` relative link in a `.md` file resolves.
- The check doesn't look for hosts or secrets, and it builds nothing.
- An index page at the repo root passes the check unchanged. An index or MkDocs home page inside
  `runbooks/` fails the "Use when" rule unless the check exempts it.
- `STANDARDS.md` has one rule: "A runbook's first line says when to use it." It says nothing about
  redaction or publishing.
- Nothing is set up yet for any format: there's no `mkdocs.yml`, no index page, and no PDF tooling.
- The project has no git remote, no CI, and no `[remote] publish` in `.claude/marathon.toml`.
- One single sign-on access group grants the docs host, the file share, and read access to this
  repository. That makes the audience the group's membership, whatever the format
  (`context/publishing.md`). So format and audience are independent, and both can be decided in
  this round.

**Currency**
- cwd: no currency command

**Questions**

1. **First edition's format: an MkDocs static site, a single PDF, or a Markdown index page in the
   repository?**
   - **rec:** an MkDocs static site on the internal docs host. Readers can search it and link to
     it, and each publish replaces the previous one, so nobody reads a stale copy. A PDF leaves
     stale copies behind after every edit. A Markdown index needs a hosted repository, and this
     project has no remote. MkDocs is the standard tool for this, so the task writes no generator
     of its own. Cost: the docs host may not load while internal DNS is down.
   - **changes:** MkDocs adds a `mkdocs.yml` and a site build that runs by hand, since there's no
     CI. The check has to exempt or move the home page so the "Use when" rule doesn't fail. A PDF
     replaces those with a PDF build and needs no change to the check. A Markdown index replaces
     them with one index page, also with no change to the check, but the repository needs a remote
     first.
2. **First edition's audience: on-call engineers only, or on-call engineers and the support team?**
   - **rec:** on-call engineers only. The five runbooks can then ship as written. Support asked
     for access in the last quarterly review. Opening the edition to them would first need a
     redaction pass over the three runbooks that name `db-primary-01.int.example.net`,
     `secret/platform/acme-token`, and `jobs-01.int.example.net`. It would also need a check rule
     that keeps new runbooks free of hosts and secrets. I'd record support's request as a backlog
     goal instead.
   - **changes:** "On-call only" leaves the access group as on-call and adds no redaction work;
     support's request goes to `backlog`. Adding support puts a redaction pass and a new check
     rule in this task, and adds support to the access group.

**reply:** "1 ok, 2 ok" or "1 yes but ..."

---

Round 2 depends on your answers. Your format answer decides who uploads the edition to the docs
host or file share, since no agent publishes outside the repository. If you add support, round 2
also covers how to redact. The Door will probably be one-way, because an edition can't be recalled
once readers have it.

This session has no file-writing tool, so I couldn't create the plan file under `.claude/plans/`
that should hold this round. If the next session doesn't pick the round up from this conversation,
it starts from your answers.
